history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: 'Vishnu Dol' with CSV town 'Sivasagar' is read as the Vishnudol on the eastern side of the Sivasagar (Borpukhuri) tank in Sivasagar town - not the Gaurisagar Vishnu Dol (built by Queen Phuleswari, c. 1715-1719, about 12 km west) nor the Joysagar Vishnu Dol (1698, Rudra Singha). Built in 1734 by Queen Madambika (Bar Raja Ambika), wife of Swargadeo Siva Singha, as part of the Shiva-Devi-Vishnu dol trio on the tank bank. Smaller than Sivadol - about 60 ft high and 120 ft in diameter - with a honeycomb-style spire and eight turrets; it faces west. The interior reflects Vaishnav influence: no deity statue or sculpture is installed, and Srimanta Sankardeva's Namghosha and other Vaishnavite books are kept in the temple. Daily worship is offered; the month of Bhada draws the largest crowds for kirtans.

name: Vishnu Dol
town_description: Sivasagar, about 370 km east of Guwahati, was the seat of Ahom power for nearly six centuries (capital Rangpur) and is a leading tea- and oil-producing centre. The 200-year-old Sivasagar tank (Borpukhuri) anchors the town, ringed by Ahom monuments such as Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar and the three dols.

travel.airport: Jorhat Airport (Rowriah), about 80 km west; Dibrugarh Airport is a longer alternative
travel.road: On the eastern part of the Sivasagar tank complex in Sivasagar town, near the tank; reachable by auto-rickshaw/three-wheeler

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (winter is pleasant, ~15 C); the Bhada month (Aug-Sep) is the busiest with kirtans
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-6:00 PM (complex timings; verify on visit)
